# What this document does

The SEIR BiLSTM in `SEIR_BiLSTM.Rmd` only reads curves of exactly 61 days, starting
at the beginning of the epidemic. This document trains one that reads **any length
from `r params$window_min` to `r params$window_max` days, starting anywhere**:

- the training epidemics are simulated for `r params$n_days` days;
- in every training batch each curve is cut to a random window: the length is drawn
  uniformly between `r params$window_min` and `r params$window_max` days (one length
  per batch), and the start uniformly over the positions where the window fits, so
  windows come from the beginning, middle and end of the epidemics;
- the network estimates `ptran`, `crate` and `R0`, as before.
- with `stop_zeros` above 0, each curve's **informative days** end at its first run
  of `stop_zeros` days without cases (7 = a week): windows are only taken from the
  informative days, the rest is ignored, and the trained model cuts new curves the
  same way. Beginning, middle and end then refer to the informative days.
- `previous_models` (model folders separated by commas) is an earlier model,
  evaluated on exactly the same windows for comparison.
- with `estimate_state`, the network also estimates the state of the epidemic at
  the start of the window: the shares of the population exposed, infectious and
  recovered. A rebuilt curve then starts from that state, wherever the window is.
- `fixed_model` (folders separated by commas are averaged) is the 61-day model it is
  compared with, named `fixed_label`.

It is then checked on new simulated epidemics, for many window lengths at the
beginning, middle and end, next to the 61-day model, and on the Utah COVID-19 data
using the last 30 to 365 days.

Everything is saved under `params$out_dir`, and re-knitting reuses the saved bank and
models. `seeds`, `ensemble`, `stop_after` and `sim_cores` work as in `SEIR_BiLSTM.Rmd`.

```r
rmarkdown::render("SEIR_variable_length_BiLSTM.Rmd", output_dir = "results/seir_variable_length")
```

```{r settings}
N_SIMS     <- params$n_sims
N_DAYS     <- params$n_days
WINDOW_MIN <- params$window_min
WINDOW_MAX <- params$window_max
EPOCHS     <- params$epochs
N_TEST     <- params$n_test
N_GRID     <- params$n_grid   # test curves used for the length x position grid
N_REPS     <- params$n_reps
RETRAIN    <- isTRUE(params$retrain)
OUT_DIR    <- params$out_dir
SIM_CORES  <- as.integer(params$sim_cores)
SEEDS      <- as.integer(params$seeds)
ENSEMBLE   <- isTRUE(params$ensemble) && length(SEEDS) > 1

BANK_SEED <- 122
TEST_SEED <- 2025

KNOWN   <- c("n", "recov", "incub")
TARGETS <- c("ptran", "crate", "R0")

# Settings of the tuned SEIR model, with the SIR reference recipe's scaling and
# output layer.
hp <- jsonlite::read_json(params$hyperparameters)
LEARNING_RATE     <- hp$learning_rate
BATCH_SIZE        <- as.integer(hp$batch_size)
HIDDEN_SIZE       <- as.integer(hp$hidden_size)
NUM_LAYERS        <- as.integer(hp$num_layers)
DROPOUT           <- hp$dropout
PHYSICS_WEIGHT    <- hp$physics_weight
# Optional overrides for long-sequence training (0 = keep the tuned value / no clipping).
if (params$learning_rate > 0) LEARNING_RATE <- params$learning_rate
GRAD_CLIP <- if (params$grad_clip > 0) params$grad_clip else NULL
STOP_ZEROS <- params$stop_zeros   # 0 = use the whole curve
ESTIMATE_STATE <- isTRUE(params$estimate_state)
STATE_NAMES    <- c("exposed_share", "infected_share", "recovered_share")
INCIDENCE_MAX     <- 10000
OUTPUT_ACTIVATION <- c("sigmoid", "softplus", "softplus")

# Window lengths and positions used to test the model.
GRID_LENGTHS <- c(30, 61, 90, 120, 180, 270, 365)
POSITIONS    <- c("beginning", "middle", "end")

dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.path = file.path(normalizePath(OUT_DIR), "figures", ""))

settings <- data.frame(
  setting = c("training simulations", "days simulated", "window lengths", "epochs",
              "test curves", "learning rate", "batch size", "hidden units", "BiLSTM layers",
              "dropout", "physics weight", "gradient clipping", "informative days end after",
              "daily cases divided by", "network seeds",
              "output folder"),
  value = c(N_SIMS, N_DAYS, paste(WINDOW_MIN, "to", WINDOW_MAX), EPOCHS, N_TEST,
            signif(LEARNING_RATE, 3), BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, NUM_LAYERS, round(DROPOUT, 3),
            signif(PHYSICS_WEIGHT, 3), if (is.null(GRAD_CLIP)) "none" else GRAD_CLIP,
            if (STOP_ZEROS > 0) paste(STOP_ZEROS, "days without cases") else "(whole curve)", INCIDENCE_MAX,
            paste(SEEDS, collapse = ", "),
            normalizePath(OUT_DIR))
)
write.csv(settings, file.path(OUT_DIR, "settings.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(settings)
```

| | 61-day SEIR model | This document |
|---|---|---|
| Simulated days | 61 | `r N_DAYS` |
| What the network reads | days 1 to 61 | any window of `r WINDOW_MIN` to `r WINDOW_MAX` days, anywhere in the epidemic |
| Training windows | the whole curve | new random windows every epoch: length and start uniform |
| Known inputs, estimated parameters, parameter ranges | `n`, `recov`, `incub`; `ptran`, `crate`, `R0`; `seir_simulator()` defaults | same |
| Network settings | tuned (hyperparameter search) | same |

The starting prevalence is not estimated: a window from the middle of an epidemic
does not start at its beginning.

# Step 1: simulate the training bank

```{r training-bank}
bank_dir   <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "training_bank")
theta_file <- file.path(bank_dir, "seir_theta.csv")
obs_file   <- file.path(bank_dir, "seir_observations.csv")
state_files_of <- function(dir) setNames(file.path(dir, paste0("seir_", STATE_NAMES, ".csv")), STATE_NAMES)

# The same epidemics as generate_seir_training_data(); with estimate_state, also
# the shares exposed, infectious and recovered at the start of each day.
simulate_bank <- function(n_sims, seed) {
  if (!ESTIMATE_STATE) return(list(bank = generate_seir_training_data(n_sims = n_sims, ndays = N_DAYS, seed = seed)))
  base <- seir_simulator(ndays = N_DAYS)
  sim  <- new_simulator(
    sample_parameters = base$sample_parameters,
    run = function(parameters, seed) {
      m <- epiworldR::ModelSEIRCONN(
        name = "sim", n = parameters$n, prevalence = parameters$preval,
        contact_rate = parameters$crate, incubation_days = parameters$incub,
        transmission_rate = parameters$ptran, recovery_rate = parameters$recov
      )
      epiworldR::verbose_off(m)
      epiworldR::run(m, ndays = N_DAYS + 1L, seed = seed)
      h <- epiworldR::get_hist_total(m)
      h <- h[order(h$date), ]
      at_start <- function(state) h$counts[h$state == state][seq_len(N_DAYS)] / parameters$n
      c(get_incidence(m, N_DAYS), at_start("Exposed"), at_start("Infected"), at_start("Recovered"))
    },
    type = "SEIR"
  )
  out <- simulate_training_data(sim, n_sims = n_sims, seed = seed)
  cols <- function(k) out$observations[, k * N_DAYS + seq_len(N_DAYS), drop = FALSE]
  list(
    bank   = new_training_data(out$theta, cols(0), type = "SEIR", source = "epiworldR ModelSEIRCONN"),
    states = setNames(lapply(1:3, cols), STATE_NAMES)
  )
}

# data.table::fwrite is much faster than write.csv for large banks.
write_matrix <- function(x, file) {
  if (requireNamespace("data.table", quietly = TRUE)) {
    data.table::fwrite(as.data.frame(round(x, 5)), file)
  } else {
    write.csv(round(x, 5), file, row.names = FALSE)
  }
}
save_bank <- function(x, dir) {
  save_training_data(x$bank, name = "seir", output_dir = dir)
  for (nm in names(x$states)) write_matrix(x$states[[nm]], state_files_of(dir)[[nm]])
}

have_bank <- file.exists(theta_file) && file.exists(obs_file) &&
  nrow(read.csv(theta_file)) == N_SIMS &&
  (!ESTIMATE_STATE || all(file.exists(state_files_of(bank_dir))))

if (have_bank) {
  train_bank <- read_training_data(theta_file, obs_file, type = "SEIR")
} else {
  sim_time <- system.time({
    sizes  <- diff(round(seq(0, N_SIMS, length.out = max(SIM_CORES, 1) + 1)))
    chunks <- parallel::mclapply(seq_along(sizes), function(k) {
      simulate_bank(sizes[k], BANK_SEED + k - 1)
    }, mc.cores = max(SIM_CORES, 1))
    failed <- vapply(chunks, inherits, logical(1), what = "try-error")
    if (any(failed)) stop("Simulation chunk(s) failed: ", paste(which(failed), collapse = ", "))
    whole <- list(
      bank = new_training_data(
        parameters   = do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, function(x) x$bank$theta)),
        observations = do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, function(x) x$bank$observations)),
        type = "SEIR", source = "epiworldR ModelSEIRCONN"
      ),
      states = if (ESTIMATE_STATE) setNames(lapply(STATE_NAMES, function(nm) {
        do.call(rbind, lapply(chunks, function(x) x$states[[nm]]))
      }), STATE_NAMES)
    )
    rm(chunks)
  })
  dir.create(bank_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  save_bank(whole, bank_dir)
  train_bank <- whole$bank
  rm(whole)
  writeLines(as.character(round(sim_time[["elapsed"]])), file.path(bank_dir, "simulation_seconds.txt"))
}
train_bank
```

How long the simulated epidemics last matters for windows taken late: a window that
starts after the epidemic is over shows no cases.

```{r epidemic-length}
# Days before the first run of k days without cases (the whole curve if none).
informative_days <- function(curve, k) {
  if (k <= 0) return(length(curve))
  r   <- rle(as.numeric(curve) == 0)
  hit <- which(r$values & r$lengths >= k)[1]
  if (is.na(hit)) length(curve) else sum(r$lengths[seq_len(hit)]) - r$lengths[hit]
}
last_case <- apply(train_bank$observations, 1, function(r) if (any(r > 0)) max(which(r > 0)) else 0)
cat("Last day with a case:\n"); print(summary(last_case))
if (STOP_ZEROS > 0) {
  active_train <- apply(train_bank$observations, 1, informative_days, k = STOP_ZEROS)
  cat("\nInformative days (before the first", STOP_ZEROS, "days without cases):\n")
  print(summary(active_train))
  cat("Share shorter than", WINDOW_MIN, "days (not used in training):",
      round(mean(active_train < WINDOW_MIN), 3), "\n")
}
```

```{r stop-after-bank, include=FALSE}
if (identical(params$stop_after, "bank")) knitr::knit_exit()
```

# Step 2: train with random windows

```{r train}
model_dirs <- file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("model_seed_", SEEDS))

model_matches <- function(dir, seed) {
  cfg_file <- file.path(dir, "model_config.json")
  if (!file.exists(file.path(dir, "model.pt")) || !file.exists(cfg_file)) return(FALSE)
  cfg <- jsonlite::read_json(cfg_file)
  cfg$epochs == EPOCHS && cfg$seed == seed && isTRUE(cfg$variable_length) &&
    cfg$window_min == WINDOW_MIN && cfg$window_max == WINDOW_MAX &&
    cfg$hidden_size == HIDDEN_SIZE && cfg$batch_size == BATCH_SIZE &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(cfg$learning_rate, LEARNING_RATE)) &&
    identical(cfg$grad_clip, GRAD_CLIP) &&
    identical(unlist(cfg$state_targets), if (ESTIMATE_STATE) STATE_NAMES else NULL) &&
    identical(is.null(cfg$window_stop_zeros), STOP_ZEROS == 0) &&
    (STOP_ZEROS == 0 || cfg$window_stop_zeros == STOP_ZEROS)
}

for (i in seq_along(SEEDS)) {
  if (RETRAIN || !have_bank || !model_matches(model_dirs[i], SEEDS[i])) {
    train_time <- system.time(train_bilstm_calibrator(
      name = "seir", known_names = KNOWN, target_names = TARGETS, type = "SEIR",
      parameter_file = theta_file, observation_file = obs_file, output_dir = model_dirs[i],
      epochs = EPOCHS, batch_size = BATCH_SIZE, learning_rate = LEARNING_RATE,
      seed = SEEDS[i], hidden_size = HIDDEN_SIZE, num_layers = NUM_LAYERS, dropout = DROPOUT,
      physics_weight = PHYSICS_WEIGHT, incidence_max = INCIDENCE_MAX,
      output_activation = c(OUTPUT_ACTIVATION, if (ESTIMATE_STATE) rep("sigmoid", length(STATE_NAMES))),
      state_files = if (ESTIMATE_STATE) state_files_of(bank_dir), device = params$device,
      window_min = WINDOW_MIN, window_max = WINDOW_MAX, grad_clip = GRAD_CLIP,
      window_stop_zeros = if (STOP_ZEROS > 0) STOP_ZEROS else NULL
    ))
    writeLines(as.character(round(train_time[["elapsed"]])), file.path(model_dirs[i], "training_seconds.txt"))
  }
}

cfg <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path(model_dirs[1], "model_config.json"))
cat("Best epoch:", cfg$best_epoch, "of", cfg$epochs, " | trained on:", cfg$device,
    " | training time:", round(as.numeric(readLines(file.path(model_dirs[1], "training_seconds.txt"))) / 60, 1), "minutes\n")
```


```{r history, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
matplot(history$epoch, history[, c("train_loss", "validation_loss")], type = "l", lty = 1,
        lwd = 2, col = c("black", "red"), log = "y", xlab = "epoch", ylab = "loss (log scale)",
        main = "Training history")
abline(v = cfg$best_epoch, lty = 2, col = "grey40")
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c("black", "red"), legend = c("train", "validation"))
plot(history$epoch, history$validation_mse_R0, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "red", log = "y",
     xlab = "epoch", ylab = "scaled MSE (log scale)", main = "R0 part of the validation loss")

par(op)
```

```{r validation-by-length}
val <- read.csv(file.path(model_dirs[1], "validation_predictions.csv"))
by_length <- aggregate(cbind(R0_abs_error = abs(pred_R0 - true_R0)) ~ window_length, val, mean)
knitr::kable(by_length, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Step 3: new simulated epidemics, by window length and position

`r format(N_TEST, big.mark = ",")` new `r N_DAYS`-day epidemics (a different seed).
For the first `r N_GRID` of them, each model gets windows of
`r paste(GRID_LENGTHS, collapse = ", ")` days taken from the **beginning** (day 1 on),
the **middle** and the **end** of `r if (STOP_ZEROS > 0) "each curve's informative days (an epidemic only counts for a length if its informative days are at least that long)" else "the curve"`.
`r if (nzchar(params$previous_models)) paste0("The earlier model (", params$previous_label, ") gets exactly the same windows.") else ""`

```{r test-bank}
test_dir        <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "test_bank")
test_theta_file <- file.path(test_dir, "seir_theta.csv")
test_obs_file   <- file.path(test_dir, "seir_observations.csv")
if (file.exists(test_theta_file) && nrow(read.csv(test_theta_file)) == N_TEST) {
  test_bank <- read_training_data(test_theta_file, test_obs_file, type = "SEIR")
} else {
  x <- simulate_bank(N_TEST, TEST_SEED)
  dir.create(test_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  if (ESTIMATE_STATE) save_bank(x, test_dir) else save_training_data(x$bank, name = "seir", output_dir = test_dir)
  test_bank <- x$bank
}
if (ESTIMATE_STATE && !all(file.exists(state_files_of(test_dir)))) {
  # An older test bank without states: simulate the states for the same curves.
  x <- simulate_bank(N_TEST, TEST_SEED)
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(x$bank$observations), unname(test_bank$observations))))
  for (nm in STATE_NAMES) write_matrix(x$states[[nm]], state_files_of(test_dir)[[nm]])
}
test_states <- if (ESTIMATE_STATE) lapply(state_files_of(test_dir), function(f) as.matrix(read.csv(f)))
truth <- test_bank$theta[seq_len(N_GRID), TARGETS]
```

```{r grid}
make_model <- function(dirs) {
  cls <- lapply(trimws(strsplit(dirs, ",")[[1]]), function(d) bilstm_calibrator(d, known_names = KNOWN, type = "SEIR"))
  if (length(cls) == 1) return(cls[[1]])
  structure(list(
    pre_process  = function(x, ...) x,
    run          = function(x, ...) rowMeans(sapply(cls, function(cl) calibrate(x, cl, ...))),
    post_process = function(x, recov = NULL, ...) derive_crate(x, recov = recov),
    type         = "SEIR"
  ), class = "calibrator")
}
seed_cals <- lapply(model_dirs, function(d) bilstm_calibrator(d, known_names = KNOWN, type = "SEIR"))
var_cal   <- if (ENSEMBLE) make_model(paste(model_dirs, collapse = ",")) else seed_cals[[1]]
VAR_LABEL <- if (ENSEMBLE) sprintf("Variable-length (average of %d seeds)", length(SEEDS)) else "Variable-length"
models <- list()
models[[VAR_LABEL]] <- var_cal
if (nzchar(params$previous_models)) models[[params$previous_label]] <- make_model(params$previous_models)

# Informative days of each test curve (the whole curve when stop_zeros = 0).
active <- apply(test_bank$observations[seq_len(N_GRID), , drop = FALSE], 1, informative_days,
                k = STOP_ZEROS)

window_start <- function(position, length, active) {
  last <- max(active, length)   # windows stay inside the informative days
  switch(position, beginning = 1, middle = floor((last - length) / 2) + 1, end = last - length + 1)
}

combos <- expand.grid(length = GRID_LENGTHS, position = POSITIONS, curve = seq_len(N_GRID),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
combos <- combos[active[combos$curve] >= combos$length, ]

grid_file <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "grid_estimates.csv")
grid <- if (file.exists(grid_file)) read.csv(grid_file) else NULL
if (!is.null(grid)) for (nm in STATE_NAMES) if (is.null(grid[[nm]])) grid[[nm]] <- NA
for (m in names(models)) {
  if (!is.null(grid) && m %in% grid$model) next
  rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(combos)), function(k) {
    L <- combos$length[k]; i <- combos$curve[k]
    st <- window_start(combos$position[k], L, active[i])
    y  <- as.numeric(test_bank$observations[i, st:(st + L - 1)])
    est <- calibrate(y, models[[m]], n = test_bank$theta$n[i], recov = test_bank$theta$recov[i],
                     incub = test_bank$theta$incub[i])
    data.frame(model = m, combos[k, ], window_start = st, window_cases = sum(y),
               ptran = est[["ptran"]], crate = est[["crate"]], R0 = est[["R0"]],
               as.list(setNames(unname(est[STATE_NAMES]), STATE_NAMES)))
  })
  grid <- rbind(grid, do.call(rbind, rows))
  write.csv(grid, grid_file, row.names = FALSE)
}
grid <- grid[grid$model %in% names(models), ]
grid$R0_abs_error <- abs(grid$R0 - truth$R0[grid$curve])

r0_tables <- lapply(setNames(names(models), names(models)), function(m) {
  g <- grid[grid$model == m, ]
  tapply(g$R0_abs_error, list(g$length, g$position), mean)[, POSITIONS, drop = FALSE]
})
write.csv(aggregate(R0_abs_error ~ model + length + position, grid, mean),
          file.path(OUT_DIR, "R0_MAE_by_length_and_position.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
for (m in names(models)) {
  print(knitr::kable(r0_tables[[m]], digits = 3,
                     caption = paste0(m, ": R0 mean absolute error, by window length (rows) and position (columns)")))
}
```

How many test epidemics each length uses, and the share of windows with fewer than
20 cases in total (little to learn from):

```{r empty-windows}
g1 <- grid[grid$model == VAR_LABEL & grid$position == "beginning", ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(length = GRID_LENGTHS,
                        epidemics = as.integer(table(factor(g1$length, levels = GRID_LENGTHS)))),
             row.names = FALSE)
g1 <- grid[grid$model == VAR_LABEL, ]
knitr::kable(tapply(g1$window_cases < 20, list(g1$length, g1$position), mean)[, POSITIONS, drop = FALSE],
             digits = 2)
```

```{r state-accuracy, eval=ESTIMATE_STATE}
# How well the start-of-window state is estimated (shares of the population).
g <- grid[grid$model == VAR_LABEL, ]
state_tab <- sapply(STATE_NAMES, function(nm) {
  truth_nm <- test_states[[nm]][cbind(g$curve, g$window_start)]
  tapply(abs(g[[nm]] - truth_nm), g$position, mean)[POSITIONS]
})
write.csv(state_tab, file.path(OUT_DIR, "state_MAE_by_position.csv"))
knitr::kable(state_tab, digits = 4,
             caption = "Mean absolute error of the estimated start-of-window shares, by position")
```

```{r grid-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
cols <- c(beginning = "black", middle = "blue", end = "red")
ymax <- max(unlist(r0_tables), na.rm = TRUE)
plot(NA, xlim = range(GRID_LENGTHS), ylim = c(0, ymax), xlab = "window length (days)",
     ylab = "R0 mean absolute error", main = "Accuracy by window length and position")
for (k in seq_along(models)) {
  tab <- r0_tables[[k]]
  for (pos in POSITIONS) {
    lines(as.numeric(rownames(tab)), tab[, pos], type = "b", pch = 16, lwd = 2, col = cols[pos], lty = k)
  }
}
legend("topright", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c(cols, "grey40", "grey40"),
       lty = c(1, 1, 1, seq_along(models)), legend = c(POSITIONS, names(models)))
```

## Next to the 61-day model

The 61-day model can only read 61 days from the beginning. On the same 61-day
windows:

```{r vs-fixed}
fixed_cal <- make_model(params$fixed_model)
curves61  <- sort(unique(grid$curve[grid$length == 61 & grid$position == "beginning"]))
fixed_R0  <- vapply(curves61, function(i) {
  calibrate(as.numeric(test_bank$observations[i, 1:61]), fixed_cal, n = test_bank$theta$n[i],
            recov = test_bank$theta$recov[i], incub = test_bank$theta$incub[i])[["R0"]]
}, numeric(1))
score <- function(est) {
  t <- truth$R0[curves61]
  c(R0_MAE = mean(abs(est - t)), R0_R2 = 1 - sum((est - t)^2) / sum((t - mean(t))^2))
}
vs_fixed <- rbind(
  data.frame(model = params$fixed_label, t(score(fixed_R0))),
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(m) {
    g <- grid[grid$model == m & grid$length == 61 & grid$position == "beginning", ]
    data.frame(model = m, t(score(g$R0[order(g$curve)])))
  }))
)
write.csv(vs_fixed, file.path(OUT_DIR, "vs_61_day_model.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(vs_fixed, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "First 61 days of the same test curves")
```

# Step 4: Utah COVID-19 data, last 30 to 365 days

The same known values as `SEIR_BiLSTM.Rmd` (`n = 5000`, `recov = 1/7`,
`incub = `r params$utah_incub``), with the model reading the last 30 up to 365 days.

```{r utah-data}
utah_file <- file.path(OUT_DIR, "utah_covid_last365days.csv")
if (!file.exists(utah_file)) {
  zip_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
  download.file("https://coronavirus-dashboard.utah.gov/Utah_COVID19_data.zip",
                zip_file, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  target <- grep("Trends_Epidemic", unzip(zip_file, list = TRUE)$Name, value = TRUE)[1]
  utah <- read.csv(unz(zip_file, target))
  unlink(zip_file)
  utah$Date <- as.Date(utah$Date)
  utah <- tail(utah[order(utah$Date), c("Date", "Daily.Cases")], N_DAYS)
  write.csv(utah, utah_file, row.names = FALSE)
}
utah <- read.csv(utah_file)
UTAH_N <- 5000; UTAH_RECOV <- 1 / 7; UTAH_INCUB <- params$utah_incub
cat("Dates:", min(utah$Date), "to", max(utah$Date), "\n")
```

```{r utah-plot-data, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
plot(as.Date(utah$Date), utah$Daily.Cases, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",
     xlab = "", ylab = "daily cases", main = "Utah, last 365 days")
```

```{r utah-estimates}
utah_est <- do.call(rbind, lapply(GRID_LENGTHS, function(L) {
  y <- tail(utah$Daily.Cases, L)
  est <- calibrate(y, var_cal, n = UTAH_N, recov = UTAH_RECOV, incub = UTAH_INCUB)
  data.frame(last_days = L, ptran = est[["ptran"]], crate = est[["crate"]], R0 = est[["R0"]],
             as.list(setNames(unname(est[STATE_NAMES]), STATE_NAMES)))
}))
if (nzchar(params$previous_models)) {
  utah_est$R0_previous <- vapply(GRID_LENGTHS, function(L) calibrate(
    tail(utah$Daily.Cases, L), models[[params$previous_label]], n = UTAH_N, recov = UTAH_RECOV,
    incub = UTAH_INCUB)[["R0"]], numeric(1))
}
utah_est$R0_61_day_model <- ifelse(
  utah_est$last_days == 61,
  calibrate(tail(utah$Daily.Cases, 61), fixed_cal, n = UTAH_N, recov = UTAH_RECOV, incub = UTAH_INCUB)[["R0"]],
  NA
)
write.csv(utah_est, file.path(OUT_DIR, "utah_estimates_by_length.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(utah_est, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

Rebuilding the last 61 and 120 days. `r if (ESTIMATE_STATE) "The simulations start from the model's own estimate of the shares exposed, infectious and recovered on the first day of the window." else "The simulations start as in SEIR_BiLSTM.Rmd: the number initially exposed is about the first day's cases times incub."`

```{r utah-reconstruct, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1))
utah_fit <- NULL
for (L in c(61, 120)) {
  y   <- tail(utah$Daily.Cases, L)
  est <- utah_est[utah_est$last_days == L, ]
  sim <- seir_simulator(ndays = L)
  pars <- list(n = UTAH_N, recov = UTAH_RECOV, incub = UTAH_INCUB, preval = y[1] * UTAH_INCUB / UTAH_N,
               ptran = est$ptran, crate = est$crate)
  if (ESTIMATE_STATE) {
    pars$preval          <- est$exposed_share
    pars$start_infected  <- est$infected_share
    pars$start_recovered <- est$recovered_share
  }
  runs <- vapply(seq_len(N_REPS), function(i) simulate_from_parameters(sim, pars, seed = i), numeric(L))
  lo <- apply(runs, 1, quantile, 0.025); hi <- apply(runs, 1, quantile, 0.975); md <- apply(runs, 1, median)
  day <- seq_len(L)
  plot(day, md, type = "n", ylim = range(c(y, lo, hi)), xlab = "day", ylab = "daily cases",
       main = sprintf("Last %d days (R0 %.2f)", L, est$R0))
  polygon(c(day, rev(day)), c(hi, rev(lo)), col = adjustcolor("red", 0.3), border = NA)
  lines(day, md, col = "red", lwd = 2)
  lines(day, y, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
  utah_fit <- rbind(utah_fit, data.frame(last_days = L, coverage_pct = 100 * mean(y >= lo & y <= hi),
                                         RMSE = sqrt(mean((md - y)^2))))
}
par(op)
write.csv(utah_fit, file.path(OUT_DIR, "utah_fit_metrics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(utah_fit, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Run-to-run variation

```{r seeds}
if (length(SEEDS) > 1) {
  seed_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(SEEDS), function(k) {
    sub <- unique(grid[grid$length == 61 & grid$position == "beginning", "curve"])
    r0  <- vapply(sort(sub), function(i) calibrate(as.numeric(test_bank$observations[i, 1:61]), seed_cals[[k]],
             n = test_bank$theta$n[i], recov = test_bank$theta$recov[i], incub = test_bank$theta$incub[i])[["R0"]],
             numeric(1))
    data.frame(model = paste("seed", SEEDS[k]),
               R0_MAE_first_61_days = mean(abs(r0 - truth$R0[sort(sub)])),
               utah_R0_last_61_days = calibrate(tail(utah$Daily.Cases, 61), seed_cals[[k]], n = UTAH_N,
                                                recov = UTAH_RECOV, incub = UTAH_INCUB)[["R0"]])
  }))
  write.csv(seed_table, file.path(OUT_DIR, "seed_variation.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  knitr::kable(seed_table, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("One seed only.\n")
}
```

# Summary

How to read it:

- **The length x position table** is the main result: how accurate `R0` is for each
  window length at the beginning, middle and end of an epidemic.
- **Windows at the end** of the whole curve often contain no cases once the epidemic
  is over; no method can estimate anything from those. With `stop_zeros`, windows
  stay inside the informative days instead.
- **Next to the 61-day model**: whether reading any length costs accuracy on the
  61-day case the old model was built for.
- **Utah**: how the estimate changes as the model reads more of the history. With
  `n = 5000`, a long run of 30 or more cases a day cannot come from one SEIR
  epidemic, so long Utah windows are outside what the model can describe.
